title: KV cache prefetch contamination leading to memory spiral and eviction instability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the March 2026 incident where background prefetch logic contaminated shard metadata and triggered a cascading memory growth and eviction instability. This ticket tracks remediation, short-term mitigations, instrumentation additions, and follow-on hardening work to prevent recurrence and restore predictable tenant isolation.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-01T03:40Z a surge in tenant A's request rate plus a new prefetch heuristic caused stale 'prefetch' entries to be inserted without proper TTLs and reference accounting. Over 18 minutes shards experienced progressive slab fragmentation and an eviction score amplification loop: eviction mis-sampling dropped hot entries while prefetch floaters prevented compaction, causing memory consumption to exceed safe thresholds and triggering capacity throttles and elevated 5xx rates for affected tenants.
timeline: 2026-03-01T03:38Z - Canary alert: elevated slab utilization on shard-17
2026-03-01T03:41Z - Autoscaler and request-throttles kicked in for tenant A; first user-facing errors observed
2026-03-01T03:50Z - On-call paged; initial mitigation: reduce prefetch worker concurrency and enable per-tenant soft caps
2026-03-01T04:10Z - Root-cause hypothesis formed: prefetch inserted entries with missing TTL & zero refcount leading to compaction skipping
2026-03-01T04:35Z - Temporary rollback of prefetch heuristic deployed; memory usage began to trend down
2026-03-01T05:05Z - Traffic normalized; incident declared mitigated; ticket created for follow-ups
investigation_notes: Repro locally by simulating a high-rate tenant with prefetch enabled; observed two failure modes: (1) prefetch inserting marker entries without namespace TTL causing namespace-level GC to ignore them, (2) compaction path skipping entries flagged as 'prefetch_candidate' because flag combined with 0 refcount produced a tombstone race. Telemetry gaps slowed diagnosis: missing per-shard prefetch origin histograms and no compact-pass skip counters. We also found that eviction scoring used stale approximate counters which were biased by prefetch churn, amplifying eviction of valid hot entries.
root_cause: A regression in the prefetch worker (runtime change in 1.21) failed to assign TTL/refcount properly for some warmed entries and introduced a 'prefetch_candidate' tag that inadvertently made compaction treat entries as ephemeral. This plus an eviction score calculation that did not account for prefetch-originated churn produced a positive feedback loop: more prefetch -> more fragmentation -> worse eviction scoring -> more misses -> more prefetch.
impact: High: multiple tenants experienced increased 5xxs and latency; autoscaler consumed reserve capacity causing pressure on Dedicated pools for ~25 minutes. No data loss observed, but cache state required forced compaction for some shards.
action_items: A: Emergency rollback landed for prefetch heuristic (completed) - OWNER: Marco Reyes - ETA: Done
B: Add strict TTL/refcount validation in prefetch path with unit + integration tests to fail CI on missing TTLs - OWNER: Priya Nair - ETA: 2026-03-12
C: Instrument per-shard prefetch-origin counters and compaction-skip metrics; expose dashboard + alert when compaction_skip_rate > 0.5% - OWNER: Jamal Ortiz - ETA: 2026-03-08
D: Adjust eviction score to discount prefetch-origin churn and add smoothing window to avoid amplification spikes - OWNER: Chen Li - ETA: 2026-03-18
E: Implement per-tenant soft memory caps that shed prefetch work before global eviction starts; include tenant-priority override for enterprise tenants - OWNER: Marco Reyes & SRE - ETA: 2026-03-22
F: Build a repair tool to recompact affected shards offline and reconcile metadata (runbook + playbook) - OWNER: Infrastructure Tools - ETA: 2026-03-25
G: Post-deployment canary plan: synthetic workload that exercises prefetch+compaction loop and validates metrics before scaling - OWNER: QE - ETA: 2026-03-10
H: Create regression tests for TTL/refcount invariants and add fuzz tests that simulate prefetch churn patterns - OWNER: Test Eng - ETA: 2026-03-15

I: Run retrospective and update runbook with checklist for similar memory-growth incidents, include quick rollback steps and emergency compaction commands - OWNER: Incident Lead (Aisha Patel) - ETA: 2026-03-09
notes: This ticket captures both short-term safety mitigations and longer-term architectural changes (eviction smoothing and tenant soft caps). Avoid re-introducing the previous prefetch heuristic until validation gates (canary + synthetic) exist. Consider backporting safe TTL/refcount checks to 1.21-1.22 maintenance branches.
postmortem_actions_status: Mitigation deployed; instrumentation and tests in progress; major refactor scheduled in Cycle 2026-W12
